title: What stopped my AI-built puzzle game from having "one shape beats every level"
author: Commercial_Cable_404
selftext:
The #1 complaint in reviews of draw-to-save games is that one shape wins everything ("just circle the hive"). With Claude Code writing the levels, adding levels was easy; knowing they were good was the hard part.

What worked: the physics is a single file that also runs in Node, so every level gets played automatically, mirror images included. The solution line has to win 20/20 with a little wobble, a sloppy copy has to win most of the time, and about 150 default shapes (domes, boxes, cages) have to mostly lose. Neighbouring levels also have to give the line a different job. Every change runs this in about a minute.

It still missed one. A Reddit player beat half the levels by cupping the hive under its branch. That became a new check, so it can't come back.

Game: Honey Line, free in the browser with ads: https://playgama.ai/play/gvawbtt52widdp
